headline: A 35% volume increase over four weeks is landing well — easy-run HR has dropped meaningfully at comparable effort, suggesting the load is building fitness rather than accumulating fatigue.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your aerobic efficiency is moving in the right direction. Easy-run heart rate has dropped substantially at comparable paces across this block, which is a clear within-athlete signal that the higher volume is being absorbed and converted — not just tolerated. That's the distinction worth noting: load can accumulate without producing adaptation, but the HR data suggests adaptation is happening.

The 20-week running streak ties your personal best, and strength work has also ticked up in frequency this block. The combination of higher running volume, improved aerobic efficiency markers, and maintained strength consistency is about as coherent a positive picture as the data can offer. No single metric is doing the heavy lifting here — they're pointing the same direction.

One thing worth holding: a 35% volume jump in four weeks is meaningful, and the current structural question is whether to extend this level or let the body consolidate before pushing further. The efficiency data is encouraging, but durability across a second consecutive elevated block deserves attention — the data looks good now, and that's exactly when it's worth being intentional rather than opportunistic.
watch_items: Monitor whether easy-run HR continues to stabilise or begins drifting upward — a sustained rise at the same effort level would be the first signal this block needs consolidation
Watch how the legs respond to back-to-back or higher-intensity efforts over the coming week, given the volume step-up is still recent
Strength streak is short at three weeks — worth noting whether session quality and recovery from lifting remains consistent as running load stays elevated
The 20-week streak is now at its personal best; pay attention to any subtle motivation or mechanical signals that distinguish a healthy streak from one being maintained at cost

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 168 km vs 125 km prior block (+35%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 144 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 9 vs 6 runs)
